la:noun:cibus.html:
cĭbus, i, m.
perh. root of capio
,
food for man and beast, victuals, fare, nutriment, fodder (class. in prose and poetry, both in sing. and plur.; syn.: esca, epulae; opp. potio,; cf. ; so, cibus potusque,: cibus et vinum,; : unda cibusque,): cibum capere,; : petere,; : capessere (of animals),: sumere,; : tantum cibi et potionis adhibendum, etc.,: digerere,; cf. : coquere,: concoquere,: mandere,: cibos suppeditare,: (Cleanthes) negat ullum esse cibum tam gravem, quin is die et nocte concoquatur,; cf.: suavissimus et idem facillimus ad concoquendum,: flentes orabant, ut se cibo juvarent,: cibus animalis,the means of nourishment in the air,: cibi bubuli,; : cibus erat caro ferina,: cum tenues hamos abdidit ante cibus,the bait,; ; .—
Transf. to the nourishment of plants, the nutritive juice, ; .—
Trop., food, sustenance (rare): quasi quidam humanitatis cibus,: cibus furoris,: causa cibusque mali,.

la:adj:cibarius.html:
cĭbārĭus, a, um, adj.
cibus
,
pertaining to or suitable for food (class.): res,: leges, i. e. sumptuary laws, laws restraining luxury, Cato ap. : uva, suitable only for eating, not for wine, ; cf.: uva vilitatis cibariae,.—
Subst.: cĭbārĭa, ōrum, n., food, nutriment, victuals, provisions, fare, ration, fodder (in the jurists a more restricted idea than alimenta, which comprises every thing necessary for sustaining life, ; cf. ; ; and in gen. the whole tit. 1: de alimentis vel cibariis legatis),; ; ; : congerere,; Dig. l. l. al.—Of soldiers, Müll.; ; ; ; cf. ; ; ; —Of the provincial magistrates, corn allowed to deputies: cibaria praefecti,; ; , §§ 216 and 217; .—Of cattle, Cato. R. R. 60; ; ; ; —In sing., .—
Meton. (in accordance with the fare given to servants), ordinary, common: panis,black bread, (cf. : panis cibarius est, qui ad cibum servis datur, nec delicatus); so subst.: cĭbā-rĭum, ii, n., also called cibarium secundarium, the coarser meal which remains after the fine wheat flour, shorts, : vinum, Varr. ap. : oleum,. 50, 18 sq.: sapor, Schneid.—
Trop.: cibarius Aristoxenus, i. e. an ordinary musician, Varr. ap. .
